messages.author: b220624aff0d88b6
messages.subject: Interpreting interaction estimate from fitqtl
parts:
Dear Dr. Karl Broman,

I have performed scantwo() on the RIL population and found significant evidence for interaction in cases case1 and case 2. When I fit the model for the pair of qtls for each case, I got a positive interaction estimate for each of them. How can I explain the direction of this interaction estimate with respect to the effect plot? 

Thank You,
Pawandeep Singh

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Interpreting interaction estimate from fitqtl
parts:
You can use fitqtl() with the argument get.ests=TRUE to get estimated additive and interaction effects for the two-QTL model.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Interpreting interaction estimate from fitqtl
parts:
The additive effect is like the average phenotype for the BB genotype - average phenotype for AA genotype, averaged across genotypes at the 2nd locus.

The interactive effect is a difference [(ave when Q1=BB and Q2=BB) - (ave when Q1=AA and Q2=BB)] - [(ave when Q1=BB and Q2=AA) - (ave when Q1=AA and Q2=AA)].

Looking at your previous figures, we have, for both cases, (ave when Q1=BB and Q2=BB) > (ave when Q1=AA and Q2=BB)
while (ave when Q1=BB and Q2=AA) < (ave when Q1=AA and Q2=AA), and so the interaction effect in both cases should be positive.

For the additive effects of the individual loci, in case 1 things look pretty close to balanced and so I'd expect the additive effects to be small, and indeed the estimates are on the order of their standard errors, so confidence intervals would overlap 0.

In case 2, things look balanced for the S9 locus, while for S6 it looks like the AA genotype has higher phenotype than the BB genotype. So I'd expect S9 to have negligible additive effect, while S6 would have a negative additive effect, and that matches what you see.

karl
